questions.prompt: After leverage is chosen, what question does Chapter 8 add?
choices: How to define the next credible objective
How to make the roadmap longer
How to avoid uncertainty entirely
questions.explanation: Chapter 8 asks what proximate objective should now guide concentrated force.

questions.prompt: Which option best describes a proximate objective in this chapter?
choices: A concrete near-term objective under uncertainty
A motivational slogan for the whole team
A complete map of every later move
questions.explanation: A proximate objective is close enough and concrete enough to guide action without claiming total foresight.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter reject false precision?
choices: Because detailed language is always wrong
Because it claims certainty the situation has not earned
Because strategy should avoid making any choices
questions.explanation: False precision is weak because it pretends the full route is already known.

questions.prompt: In the school examples, what should the team name before asking for more work?
choices: The next objective that can guide immediate choices
Every task for the rest of the year
A broader mission statement
questions.explanation: The chapter pushes teams to identify a concrete next objective rather than hide inside broad aspiration.

questions.prompt: What is the main weakness of vague ambition in this chapter?
choices: It sounds too pessimistic
It gives force no usable destination
It makes work happen too quickly
questions.explanation: Vague ambition cannot guide tradeoffs because it does not identify the next objective clearly enough.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 8 relate to Chapter 7?
choices: It replaces leverage with task management
It explains what near-term objective should receive concentrated force
It argues that concentration is unnecessary
questions.explanation: Chapter 7 chose where force should matter; Chapter 8 chooses the next objective that should now guide that force.

questions.prompt: A household plan has a giant wish list but no clear next move. What would this chapter ask for?
choices: A bigger list with more details
A proximate objective that can be pursued now
A longer delay until certainty arrives
questions.explanation: The chapter favors a near-term objective that is concrete enough to guide action right now.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest sign that a proximate objective is real?
choices: It is close enough to guide current tradeoffs and action
It covers every later move already
It makes the strategy sound more inspiring
questions.explanation: A real proximate objective is concrete, near-term, and strategically meaningful enough to discipline choices.

questions.prompt: Why can a plan with many tasks still drift?
choices: Because tasks are always useless
Because detail automatically creates confusion
Because tasks do not replace a strategic near-term objective
questions.explanation: The chapter distinguishes a strategic proximate objective from mere task churn.

questions.prompt: What chapter move naturally follows proximate objectives?
choices: Turning toward design and coordinated action
Returning to vague ambition
Waiting until uncertainty disappears
questions.explanation: Once the next objective is clear, later chapters can ask how design and coordinated moves preserve coherence beyond it.
